exact_missing_items: HITL now contains two contract eras: older request-local (HITLRequest with tier_id, tier_type, allowed_actions[]) and newer runtime-facing (waiting_approval as blocked overlay, allowed_action_ids[], cmd.runtime.*)
Move approval anchoring onto canonical runtime identity: run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence, attempt_id?, plus execution-unit context refs
Add an explicit approval-scope field or object, likely approval_scope_key, so reusable approvals and one-off blocked-episode approvals cannot bleed together
Add durable approver identity fields to approval/rejection records/events so audit/history can explain who approved or declined
Deprecated allowed_actions[] is compatibility-only and MUST NOT appear in new canonical schemas
Reconcile GitHub command table with UI_Command_Catalog.md: align arg shapes for cmd.github.connect, cmd.github.disconnect, and any overlapping command definitions
Add a declared-capability mechanism to CLI_Bridged_Providers.md so bridged providers can announce multi-account, switch-notification, and attribution capabilities the same way direct providers do
Bind GitHub_API_Auth_and_Flows.md to stable account_id instead of mutable login and add account-health / degraded-capability model

Rewrite GitHub_Integration.md account UX to include: effective-account display, account-switch-reason display, requested-vs-effective admin-capability contrast, blocked-recovery-request trigger linking to canonical concern record
The canonical minimum field set is: `target_kind`; `project_id`; one canonical target selector (`subject_id` OR `object_kind` + `object_id`)
The narrow scope-restoration fields are: `focused_run_id`; `thread_id`
The narrow focus-refinement fields are: `tab_id`; `inspector_target`
Full bounded shape: `target_kind`, `project_id`, `focused_run_id`, `thread_id`, `tab_id`, `subject_id`, `object_kind`, `object_id`, `inspector_target`
`project_id` is required. Exactly one canonical target selector is required.

What is NOT a base `route_target` field: `usage_event_ref`, `wizard_id`, `wizard_step`, `message_id`, `artifact_id`, `document_id`, `workflow_run_id`, `scheduler_pass_id`, `safe_point_id`, `remediation_root_id`, `line`, `range`, per-surface state (`active_subview`, compare target, panel layout, browser tab state, widget layout)
The canonical selector rule is: exactly one primary selector is present: `subject_id` OR `object_kind` + `object_id`
`subject_id` wins for openable/renderable content subjects.
`object_kind` + `object_id` wins for domain/runtime/governance objects.
`tab_id`, `focused_run_id`, `thread_id`, and `inspector_target` never replace primary selector identity.
`project_id` is required scope, not selector identity.

Resolution order: (1) restore project_id, (2) restore route scope (focused_run_id, thread_id), (3) restore destination class from target_kind, (4) resolve primary selector (subject_id OR object_kind+object_id), (5) apply narrow focus refinement (tab_id, inspector_target)
Reject multi-selector route payloads as non-canonical. Normalize all special-case ids into `subject_id` or `object_kind` + `object_id` before they enter the canonical route layer.
blocked_sequence should be owned by the runtime scheduler/executor layer, not by UI/HITL/chat/storage
blocked_sequence scope: monotonic per {run_id, node_id}, starts at 1, increments only when node transitions from non-blocked to a new blocked episode
Make Executor_Protocol.md + Contracts_V0.md the joint owners of blocked_sequence minting semantics, blocked-episode lifecycle, and startup-recovery scheduler handshake
Recast HITL request contracts so request_id is explicitly subordinate to blocked-episode identity
canonical_replacement_hints: object_kind + object_id for wizard_id, message_id, usage_event, scheduler_pass_id, safe_point_id, remediation_root_id
object_kind + object_id for all listed special-case IDs
request_id (lookup metadata only, not canonical recovery target)
